title: Build a backward-walking engine with array rules
brief: Write the two-sided slope check, the multiply rule, the backward walk, unbroadcast, the matrix-product rule, and the ReLU rule, so slopes flow through a layer that multiplies, adds a bias, and bends.
hints: central_difference is one line: (f(x + h) - f(x - h)) / (2 * h).

In __mul__, the slope that reaches self is out.grad times other.value, and the slope that reaches other is out.grad times self.value. Use += for both, because a * a puts the same tensor in both places.

In backward, build the order with a depth-first walk that appends a node only after all of its children have been appended, and keep a visited set of id(node) so a shared node is appended once. Then set self.grad to ones and call _backward_fn on every node in reversed order.

unbroadcast: first sum over leading axes until grad has as many dimensions as shape, then sum with keepdims=True over every axis where shape has size 1 and grad does not. Then wrap the contributions in __add__ and __mul__ with it.
For out = self @ other: self.grad += out.grad @ other.value.T and other.grad += self.value.T @ out.grad. If a shape does not fit, you transposed the wrong factor.
For relu, the slope passes where the input was positive: self.grad += out.grad * (self.value > 0).
